red_flags: Told the tenant no photo came through, although the reply probably carried the photo as an attachment that the event text doesn't show
Didn't forward the reading to the landlord, which is what the human did within hours
Didn't escalate or ask a human to open the email and check for an attachment
Stored a phone number from an email signature as a profile fact, which is unnecessary
reasoning: The tenant replied 3 minutes after the chase, and the reference shows the photo was forwarded to the landlord about 3 hours later. So the reply almost certainly carried the photo as an attachment, which the event text didn't show. The agent concluded the photo was missing, emailed the tenant to resend it and held the ticket for 7 days. That was safe and low-risk, with no landlord money or safety issue involved. But it was probably wrong, and it could annoy the tenant. A better step would have been to flag that the reply may hold an attachment and have a human check it, or to forward the reading to the landlord. The agent did not forward anything and did not escalate. The profile-fact writes were harmless, but the phone number one was unnecessary. The outcome was a partial miss.
